source_refs.note: Topic 6.4.3.1 (PDF 164, printed 161). The book calls crypto transactions private; the pseudonymity, volatility and legal-status notes are general knowledge, flagged.

blocks.text: Cryptocurrencies offer a decentralized way to exchange money: instead of being issued by banks, they use blockchain to record transactions in a way that cannot be changed, without middlemen. Bitcoin, Ethereum and others let people send money quickly and cheaply, even across borders, and can include people without access to banks.
Such transactions are private because they need no personal information.
